findings.finding: The question names the answer it wants, so people will tell you about the thing you asked for rather than what actually happened to them.
findings.suggestion: Try asking for a moment that stuck with them and letting them say why, rather than naming the reason in the question.

findings.finding: One corner reads as the obviously right answer, which turns the other two into decoys nobody will choose.
findings.suggestion: Reword the three so that each is a real cost as well as a real gain, and none of them is the one a good worker is supposed to pick.

findings.finding: One end of this slider is plainly good and the other plainly bad, so it will collect agreement rather than experience.
findings.suggestion: Make both ends things a reasonable person might want, so the placement records a trade-off instead of a verdict.

findings.finding: This label runs longer than about six words, which is more than most people read on a phone before placing a marker.
findings.suggestion: Shorten it to the few words that carry the question, and leave the rest to the corners.
